title: Luciferianism

slides.text: How did a Babylonian king become Lucifer?

image.title: Isaiah's vision of the Lord's glory (Isaiah 6.1) and other scenes from the book of Isaiah. Etching by J. and J. Klauber.

slides.text: The Hebrew says Helel ben Shachar, shining one, son of dawn. It is a taunt against Babylon's king. Jerome rendered it lucifer.

image.title: Latin Vulgate Bible
image.credit: Latin Vulgate Bible — Art Institute of Chicago (public domain)

slides.text: Later exegetes fused that verse with Christ's words: I saw Satan fall like lightning from heaven. The fallen king became an angel.

slides.text: Yet the title was never only infernal. Christ calls himself the bright and morning star. The light-bearer had two faces.

slides.text: The Luciferian archetype is older than the name. Prometheus stole fire for humanity. Zeus chained him to a rock for it.

caption:
One Latin word.
One taunt against a dead king.
From it, a fallen angel.

Isaiah's shining one, son of dawn, became Jerome's lucifer.
Exegetes chained him to Satan's fall.
Centuries later, others unchained him.

Thomas Karlsson led initiates down the shadow Tree of Life.
Michael W. Ford built a theology of will and gnosis.
Asenath Mason opened the gates to anyone who would walk through.

The Luciferian does not kneel.
He steals fire, like Prometheus.
He builds what outlasts the body.

Myth, scripture, Qliphoth, and the scholars who traced how light was demonised.

The full entry waits in the Forbidden Library: alloccult.com/left-hand-path/luciferianism

review_log.summary: Strong, accurate carousel with fitting public-domain images. One blocking issue: the caption calls Jerome's 'lucifer' a mistranslation. It was a faithful Latin rendering of Helel ('shining one'), following the Septuagint's Heosphoros. The demonisation came from later exegesis, as slide 3 itself says. There is also one non-blocking Hesiod nuance on slide 5.
fixes: caption: 'One mistranslated taunt' is a popular myth a knowledgeable reader would reject. Jerome's lucifer accurately renders Helel, the shining one or morning star, as the Septuagint's Heosphoros did before him. The shift to Satan came from later exegesis, not from translation.

review_log.summary: Strong, accurate carousel. The philology follows the Round 1 fix: Helel ben Shachar, Jerome's lucifer, and later exegesis via Luke 10:18. Dates and founders match the archive page (Dragon Rouge 1989, eleven grades; Temple of Ascending Flame 2012, thirteen aspects). Images are all relevant period engravings or woodcuts, and the classical nudity is not gratuitous. One non-blocking polish note on slide 5: Hesiod has Prometheus bound to a pillar, not a rock. Ready to post.
